Implement Partner Referrals onboarding, merchant-integrations status checks, and consent webhooks
Call seller APIs with the PayPal-Auth-Assertion header once consent exists

approval.cost: No fee for app creation, review, or partner approval is stated in the documentation read (PayPal's separate Partner Program offers a 'PayPal Directory' listing at its Gold tier, documented on paypal.com partner pages outside developer.paypal.com)
approval.trigger: Two separate gates. (1) Log in with PayPal: 'Because Log in with PayPal involves sharing customer data, PayPal must review your app and approve it, before it can go live. All scopes require PayPal's approval.' Mechanics: 'For live apps, once you finish configuring Log in with PayPal and select the Save button, your application is automatically submitted for review. The review process typically takes a few weeks.' (Sandbox apps are exempt: no review needed, enabled on Save.) The PayPal privacy and security team also reviews your privacy policy and user agreement URLs, which are required to activate the feature. (2) Partner/platform: 'Fill out this form to tell us about your platform and business... A PayPal representative will evaluate your business needs and contact you about your approval.' 'You must be an approved partner to use this integration.' Go-live is manual: 'Contact your PayPal representative to go live after you've tested your integration... When you have completed the integration checklist, a PayPal representative can copy your sandbox configuration to your live account.' Seller-side vetting is separate: each onboarded seller's product provisioning carries a riskStatus (SUBSCRIBED, SUBSCRIBED_WITH_LIMIT, IN_REVIEW, NEED_MORE_DATA, DENIED), and a seller is not fully usable until onboarding completes (account created + permissions granted + email confirmed). No numeric user/seller caps are stated; the functional pre-approval cap is absolute.
approval.wait: Log in with PayPal review: 'typically takes a few weeks' (stated). Partner approval: not stated

blockers.detail: Client credentials authenticate YOU; a SaaS that needs to act in customers' accounts must use partner onboarding (payments) or Log in with PayPal (identity). There is no documented 'any developer can OAuth-connect any PayPal account for general API access' flow equivalent to Square's.
blockers.howToClear: Decide which of the three mechanisms your product actually is before building: identity, merchant payments, or first-party API use.
blockers.title: The plain REST app is not a connect product

blockers.detail: No approved-partner status means no live onboarding; live configuration is literally copied from sandbox by a PayPal representative, and Platform Partner App settings changes go through a sales manager ('To change these settings, contact your PayPal sales manager'). Timelines are entirely unstated.
blockers.howToClear: Start the partner application at the beginning of the project and build in sandbox while it proceeds.
blockers.title: Partner approval is relationship-gated, not self-serve

blockers.detail: For Log in with PayPal, 'if you change the Return URL in the Developer Dashboard, PayPal must review your app again. The review period automatically begins any time the return URL changes'. Separately, scopes are split between URL and dashboard: the scope parameter must include openid, but the actual user attributes are selected in the app's Advanced Settings; if you intend payouts/withdrawals you must select Email, Account verification status, and PayPal account ID.
blockers.howToClear: Freeze the Return URL and the dashboard attribute set before submitting for review.
blockers.title: Return URL changes re-trigger review

flavor.recommended: Depends on the job: Log in with PayPal (OpenID Connect) for identity/user data; Partner Referrals onboarding as an approved partner for acting on merchants' accounts
flavor.why: PayPal has three distinct documented mechanisms, and conflating them is the main integration trap. The object is a REST API app created in the Developer Dashboard under Apps & Credentials, yielding a Client ID and Secret, with separate Sandbox and Live instances. Log in with PayPal is an OpenID Connect flow enabled per-app ('Other features' > Log in with PayPal > Advanced Settings); the requested user attributes are configured IN THE DASHBOARD app settings in addition to the scope parameter. Partner onboarding uses a Platform REST app plus the Partner Referrals API: you POST referral data with integration_type 'THIRD_PARTY' and features (e.g. PAYMENT, REFUND), PayPal returns a one-time action_url signup link, the seller grants the features, and afterwards you call APIs on the seller's behalf using YOUR OWN access token plus a PayPal-Auth-Assertion header (a JWT with iss = your client ID and payer_id = the merchant): 'To use this header, you must get consent to act on behalf of a merchant.'

humanMust: Create a PayPal developer account and the REST app(s) in the Developer Dashboard (Sandbox and Live separately)
For Log in with PayPal: configure the feature and Advanced Settings (Return URL, attributes, privacy policy and user agreement URLs) and Save, which submits the live app for review
For merchant onboarding: submit PayPal's platform form and be approved as a partner, then work with a PayPal representative to copy the sandbox configuration to live
name: PayPal
nuances: Onboarding isn't binary: a seller can return with permissionsGranted=true yet still be unusable if email is unconfirmed or product vetting is IN_REVIEW / NEED_MORE_DATA / SUBSCRIBED_WITH_LIMIT ('feature limitation, such as a transaction limit'). Check GET /v1/customer/partners/{partner_id}/merchant-integrations/{seller_id} (account created, permissions granted, email confirmed, payments_receivable true, and the oauth_integrations block showing granted scopes) before transacting. Consent is revocable and observable: MERCHANT.ONBOARDING.COMPLETED and MERCHANT.PARTNER-CONSENT.REVOKED webhooks.

Log in with PayPal access tokens: expires_in 28800, 'The default is 28800 seconds or 8 hours', for both authorization-code and refresh-token responses. The client-credentials reference states no fixed lifetime (a sample response shows expires_in 31668, ~8.8 hours, sample value only).

Partner Referrals forks matter: integration_type 'FIRST_PARTY' (seller shares their own REST API credentials, protected by a seller_nonce; used e.g. by downloadable shopping-cart onboarding) vs 'THIRD_PARTY' (OAuth-style feature grants; the seller's scopes are recorded under oauth_third_party). Choosing the wrong type changes what you receive. The action_url 'expires after one use'; refresh it via the referral's self link or a new Partner Referrals call. Include your PayPal-Partner-Attribution-Id (BN code) on referral calls.

Legacy endpoint split: pre-January 2018 Log in with PayPal integrations use /signin/authorize; current integrations use /connect. 'PayPal recommends that new apps integrate with OpenID Connect. Apps integrated with OpenID will continue to work, but won't receive new features.' Sandbox testing uses generated Sandbox test accounts, never real accounts.

Some Platform Partner App settings are not self-serve at all: 'To change these settings, contact your PayPal sales manager.' No self-serve app-store/marketplace listing process for REST apps is described in the developer documentation read.
prerequisites: A PayPal developer account; Sandbox and Live REST apps
For Log in with PayPal: Privacy policy URL and User agreement URL (reviewed by PayPal's privacy and security team)
For partner onboarding: an approved partner application and a PayPal representative relationship

steps.detail: Developer Dashboard > Apps & Credentials > Create App; copy the Client ID and Secret. Create Sandbox apps for testing and a Live app for production; sandbox testing uses generated Sandbox test accounts (Testing Tools > Sandbox Accounts), never real accounts.
steps.title: Create the REST app(s)

steps.detail: On the app, under 'Other features', check Log in with PayPal > Advanced Settings: enter the Return URL (must exactly match the redirect_uri you send), select the user-information attributes to request (Full name, Email, Account verification status, PayPal account ID, etc.), and enter Privacy policy URL and User agreement URL. For live apps, selecting Save automatically submits the app for review ('typically takes a few weeks'; all scopes require approval). Sandbox apps skip review.
steps.time: Review typically takes a few weeks (stated)
steps.title: (Identity) Configure Log in with PayPal; Save submits for review

steps.detail: Point your button at www.paypal.com/connect?flowEntry=static&client_id=...&response_type=code&scope=... (must include openid) &redirect_uri=...&state=... The user logs in and consents; exchange the code at POST api-m.paypal.com/v1/oauth2/token (Basic auth, grant_type=authorization_code), then call GET /v1/identity/oauth2/userinfo. Refresh later with grant_type=refresh_token.
steps.title: (Identity) Implement the /connect flow

steps.detail: 'Fill out this form to tell us about your platform and business... A PayPal representative will evaluate your business needs and contact you about your approval.' Create the Platform REST app in your sandbox API caller account and subscribe to the MERCHANT.ONBOARDING.COMPLETED and MERCHANT.PARTNER-CONSENT.REVOKED webhooks.
steps.title: (Merchants) Get approved as a partner; create the Platform app

steps.detail: POST /v2/customer/partner-referrals with your client-credentials token and PayPal-Partner-Attribution-Id (your BN code): products (e.g. EXPRESS_CHECKOUT or PPCP), operations with integration_type 'THIRD_PARTY' and the features the seller will grant, legal_consents (SHARE_DATA_CONSENT), optional tracking_id. Redirect the seller to the returned one-time action_url; the seller signs up/logs in, grants the features, and confirms their email. Verify completion via the merchant-integrations API, then call seller APIs with your access token plus the PayPal-Auth-Assertion JWT (iss = your client ID, payer_id = the merchant).
steps.title: (Merchants) Onboard sellers via Partner Referrals

steps.detail: 'Contact your PayPal representative to go live after you've tested your integration... When you have completed the integration checklist, a PayPal representative can copy your sandbox configuration to your live account.' Share the email addresses and client IDs for your sandbox and live accounts with your representative.
steps.title: (Merchants) Go live via your PayPal representative

tagline: Three mechanisms that are easy to conflate: a plain REST app only ever acts as you, Log in with PayPal needs a PayPal app review that typically takes a few weeks, and acting on merchants' accounts requires becoming an approved PayPal partner first, then onboarding each seller through Partner Referrals. The old NVP/SOAP permissions path is deprecated.

time.active: ~10 min of app setup + flow code (identity) or an integration project (partner onboarding)
time.total: Weeks for Log in with PayPal review (stated 'typically takes a few weeks'); partner approval duration not stated
time.waiting: App review: typically a few weeks (stated); partner approval: not stated
